# Publisher

A publisher wakes instances from outside events. Rimsky calls you to start and stop watches; you push messages back into the control API.

A sensor is a publisher that observes external state — a schedule, an HTTP endpoint, an object store, an inbound webhook. Rimsky ships four sensor kinds: `cron`, `http`, `object-store`, and `webhook`. Write your own kind and it works the same way.

Proto file: `publisher.proto`.

## The RPCs

| RPC | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Capabilities(google.protobuf.Empty) → PublisherCapabilities` | Advertise the kinds you support |
| `Subscribe(SubscribeRequest) → SubscribeResponse` | Start a watch |
| `Unsubscribe(UnsubscribeRequest) → UnsubscribeResponse` | Stop a watch |
| `ListSubscriptions(google.protobuf.Empty) → ListSubscriptionsResponse` | Report every watch you hold |

## Advertising yourself

`PublisherCapabilities` fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `supported_kinds` | One `PublisherKindCapability` per kind you serve. Must be non-empty. |
| `protocols` | Must include `publisher`. |
| `validation_supported_roles` | The roles you answer on the `Validation` mix-in |

Each `PublisherKindCapability` carries a `kind` string and `config_schema` bytes. The schema is JSON Schema describing what a template author may write under `publishers[].config` for that kind. Leave it empty to accept anything; when you set it, it must parse as JSON.

An operator declares you under `publishers.<name>` with an `endpoint`, and optionally `observability_endpoint`, `protocols`, and `tls`.

## Subscribing

A template declares its watches in a `publishers` block, each entry carrying `name`, `kind`, `message_type`, and `config`. When an instance of that template starts, rimsky resolves the config against the instance's parameters and calls `Subscribe`.

`SubscribeRequest` fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `publisher_subscription_id` | Rimsky's id for this watch. Your key for it. |
| `instance_id` | The instance to push messages to |
| `kind` | Which of your kinds to run |
| `resolved_config` | The template author's config, resolved against the instance |
| `message_type` | The message type to send |

`Subscribe` must be idempotent. Rimsky repeats it on the same `publisher_subscription_id` after a restart and when it reconciles, and a repeat must leave one watch running rather than two.

`Unsubscribe` takes the `publisher_subscription_id` alone and stops the watch. It must also be idempotent: a second `Unsubscribe` on an id you have already stopped must succeed.

Field 5, `target_node`, is reserved on both `SubscribeRequest` and `PublisherSubscriptionDescriptor`. Do not send it.

## ListSubscriptions

`ListSubscriptions` is your restart-reconciliation surface, so answer it truthfully. Rimsky calls it, compares your answer against the watches it expects you to hold, re-subscribes for anything missing, and unsubscribes anything you hold that it no longer expects.

Each `PublisherSubscriptionDescriptor` must echo the subscription exactly: `publisher_subscription_id`, `instance_id`, `kind`, `resolved_config` byte-for-byte, `message_type`, and a non-zero `started_at`. A descriptor whose fields drift from what rimsky sent is a conformance failure, and so is an unset `started_at`.

## Pushing messages

Post the message to the control API. This is an ordinary authenticated HTTP call, not part of the gRPC protocol.

```
POST ${RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL}/v1/instances/${instance_id}/messages
Authorization: Bearer ${RIMSKY_API_KEY}
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: ${your key}

{
  "type": "system/heartbeat",
  "payload": { "...": "..." },
  "sender": "my-publisher",
  "publisher_subscription_id": "..."
}
```

The `Idempotency-Key` header is required. A retry with the same key replays instead of sending twice. The route needs the `message:send` grant on your api-key. It answers with `{"message_id": "..."}`.

`type` must be a message type the instance's template accepts. Set `sender` to your publisher's name and `publisher_subscription_id` to the id rimsky gave you, so operators can trace a message back to the watch that produced it.

The shipped `publisherkit.Send` helper does the posting for you. It makes up to three attempts, backing off between them, and it distinguishes a permanent rejection from a retriable failure: a 4xx status other than 408 and 429 stops the retries and returns a rejection.

## Egress

Guard any outbound call you make on a caller-supplied or template-supplied URL. The bundled HTTP sensor blocks loopback, private, link-local, unique-local, and multicast destinations by default, checks the resolved IP at connect time so redirects and DNS rebinding are covered, and allows only the `http` and `https` schemes. An operator opens a range back up by naming a CIDR in an allowlist environment variable, and a malformed entry stops the service at startup.

## Observability

There is no publisher observability protocol. `PublisherObservability` does not exist, and neither does a publisher entry on rimsky's observability read routes. A `publishers.<name>.observability_endpoint` key parses and starts, and rimsky reads nothing from it — the two observability protocols rimsky ships are `ExecutorObservability` and `ClaimProducerObservability`. Give your publisher its own logs and metrics rather than expecting a rimsky dashboard to show it.

## Proving it

```
rimsky conformance publisher \
  --endpoint grpc://localhost:9202 \
  --kind cron \
  --resolved-config '{"schedule":"* * * * *"}' \
  --instance-id <id> \
  --control-api http://localhost:8080
```

The suite runs seven checks: `Capabilities` (kind advertised, `publisher` in `protocols`, config schema parses), `Subscribe`, `ListSubscriptions` (every field echoed, `started_at` set), `SubscribeIdempotent`, `MessagePush`, `Unsubscribe` (the subscription disappears), and `UnsubscribeIdempotent`.

`MessagePush` runs only when you pass both `--instance-id` and a control-API URL, through `--control-api` or the `RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL` environment variable. The runner then polls the instance's messages until yours arrives. `--message-type` names the type it watches for; it defaults to `system/conformance`.

The suite requires gRPC. There is no HTTP+JSON bridge for `Publisher`.
